verdict.rationale: AnyDesk's own CLI documentation shows an admin can preconfigure credentials during deployment. A batch script installs AnyDesk, registers the license and sets a password, and this works across many devices without manual setup on each machine. However, the evidence never explicitly says that a preset password lets incoming sessions connect without someone at the host accepting them, so the 'no one has to accept' half is only implied. missing for 10: explicit documentation of unattended-access behavior (connecting without accept prompts), permission/profile configuration for unattended sessions, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can set up unattended access to a machine with credentials configured in advance, so no one has to sit at the host to accept

citations.quote: The following example batch script installs AnyDesk, registers the license key, and sets a password
Automating tasks such as installation, licensing, password setup, and removal
You can use CLI commands with software deployment tools to install and configure AnyDesk on multiple devices, without manual setup on each machine.
